title: Use Audience Projection to Let People Discover Your Feedback
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Opens with a joke about a customer asking a waiter to taste the soup rather than being told it's cold, to illustrate that self-discovered feedback lands differently than feedback simply delivered. Argues that when people generate their own conclusions, the insight feels like their own idea rather than someone else's judgment, making it stick longer and provoke less defensiveness. The technique offered is 'audience projection' -- asking a team member to imagine how a specific other person (a reader, a novice, a customer) would react to their work, prompting self-discovery through targeted questions rather than direct correction.
points: Self-discovered feedback is internalized more deeply than delivered feedback because it feels like the recipient's own idea, not someone else's judgment.
'Audience projection' -- asking someone to imagine how a specific other person would react to their work -- engineers moments of self-realization without direct correction.
The technique isn't a replacement for direct feedback in every case, but an essential option alongside it, since self-discovery beats instruction 'nearly every time.'
quotes: Telling someone the answer and letting them arrive at it themselves has a markedly different impact.
In life, when people discover feedback rather than receive it, they become less defensive, incorporate the learning faster, and retain the feedback longer.
Self-discovered insights feel like your idea, not someone else’s judgment.
Through targeted questions, leaders can guide team members to generate their own feedback, often experiencing an “aha” moment without ever offering a direct statement.
The key is for leaders to find an audience that can serve as a foil for self-discovery. Most situations and issues have a natural audience.
Self-discovery beats instruction, correction, and direct feedback nearly every time. When people generate their own feedback, it usually lands deeper, lasts longer, and leads to real change.
